sourceLabel: Roll call · Ohio House floor votes (Ohio Legislature)

rollCalls.title: Prohibit specified actions with intent to steal a motor vehicle
rollCalls.summary: Gas and diesel fuel tax. Reduces the tax on gasoline and diesel fuel for a period of three months, from 38.5 ¢ per gallon for gasoline and 47¢ per gallon for diesel to 0.01¢ per gallon for either. Prohibits a licensed retail dealer or licensed motor fuel dealer from selling motor fuel during the temporary reduction period without passing the full benefit of the reduced tax onto the consumer or other purchaser. Provides that violation of the prohibition may be considered in any licensing determination made by the Tax Commissioner and referred to the Attorney General (AG).

rollCalls.title: Revise non-recourse litigation funding agreement regulations
rollCalls.summary: Overview. Repeals the law governing nonrecourse civil litigation advance contract s and replaces it with two subsets of regulations: one for commercial litigation financing agreements (“commercial agreements ”) and another for consumer legal funding agreements (“consumer agreements”). Contract requirements. Retains the majority of the contract-related requirements under former law, but limits application of those requirements to consumer agreements, i.e., contracts with an individual that resides in Ohio for less than $400,000.

rollCalls.title: Regards entities providing behind-the-meter utility services
Regards the sale of used catalytic converters
rollCalls.summary: Requires scrap metal dealers and other persons who purchase used catalytic converters to comply with certain additional recordkeeping, reporting, and process requirements. Imposes a penalty not to exceed $7,500 on a business entity that violates the above requirements. Expands the investigatory authority and noninvestigatory responsibilities of the Director of Public Safety relating to scrap metal dealers and other persons purchasing used catalytic converters. Prohibits a motor vehicle salvage dealer from purchasing or accepting catalytic converters.

rollCalls.title: Regards drone use by law enforcement; aviation facilities
rollCalls.summary: Criminal evidence derived from a UAV. Generally, requires a peace officer to obtain a court-issued search warrant to collect surveillance data using an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) if the peace officer otherwise would need a warrant to physically enter the house or place in person to conduct the search. Prohibits surveillance data and any information obtained from that data from being admitted as evidence in a criminal proceeding if it was gathered under circumstances that required a warrant and the warrant was not obtained.

rollCalls.title: Establish the Ohio Defense Commission
rollCalls.summary: Establishes the Ohio Defense and Space Advisory Commission. Establishes the Defense and Aerospace Industry Expansion Program under which the Department of Development may make grants to support economic development related to the defense industry. Requires any entity that receives a grant under the program undergo an audit of the project administration. Makes an appropriation.

rollCalls.title: Alter amusement ride classification for inspection fee purposes
rollCalls.summary: Amusement rides. Reclassifies the types of amusement rides for purposes of re-determining each ride ’s annual inspection and reinspection fee. Decreases the annual permit fee for an inflatable ride. Creates a formula to calculate the inspection and reinspection fee for an inflatable ride based on the number of rides that are inspected at the same time at the same location and owned by the same owner instead of a flat $104 fee per inflatable ride. Food regulation laws. Exempts a registered bakery from the requirement to obtain a frozen food facility license.

rollCalls.title: Regards the operation of public schools and the DEW
rollCalls.summary: State Board of Education. Increases the number of appointed State Board of Education members from five to seven. Requires the State Board, in some circumstances, to add additional grade levels to alternative resident educator license holders ’ licenses as requested by the educator ’s employing school district. Requires the State Board to automatically revoke or deny the renewal of any license issued to an individual who pleads guilty to, is found guilty of, or is convicted of domestic violence, strangulation, or grooming.

rollCalls.title: Enact Katelyn's Law
rollCalls.summary: Creates the offense of “moving or removing human remains ” and specifies that there is no period of limitations for the offense. Provides exceptions to the offense of “moving or removing human remains” and “abuse of a corpse” relating to a woman who experiences a spontaneous miscarriage or stillbirth. Creates a specification for moving or removing human remains with a five-year mandatory prison term for an adult and a one to three-year mandatory term for a delinquent child. Names the bill’s provisions “Katelyn’s Law.”.

rollCalls.title: Waive ID, birth certificate fees for homeless individuals
rollCalls.summary: Absent voting by mail. Would have required an elector to provide photo identification ( ID) to vote by mail beginning with the November 2027, general election. Would have exempted certain electors from that requirement and provided alternative ID procedures for them. Would have allowed an elector to fulfill the photo ID requirement by providing it either when applying for ballots or when returning voted ballots to the board. Would have permitted an elector to show photo ID at the board’s office instead of making a copy.

rollCalls.title: Regards physician supervision of imaging contrast administration
rollCalls.summary: Administration of contrast – physician supervision. Revises the law authorizing a radiologist assistant to administer contrast media under the on-site supervision of a physician who is a radiologist, by also permitting the radiologist assistant to do so under the radiologist’s remote supervision. Authorizes a registered nurse, radiographer, radiation therapy technologist, and nuclear medicine technologist to administer contrast under the direct or general supervision of a physician.

rollCalls.title: Regards DoDD authority re: community capital assistance funds
rollCalls.summary: Requires the Director of Developmental Disabilities to adopt rules establishing a process for the Department of Developmental Disabilities to make available community capital assistance funds for county boards of developmental disabilities to acquire housing for individuals receiving supported living services.

rollCalls.title: Issue medical marijuana processor cultivation, dispensary license
rollCalls.summary: Establishes the paired cultivator license, its eligibility requirements, authorized activities, and restrictions under the Division of Cannabis Control (DCC). Requires DCC to issue the paired cultivator license and a dispensary license to applicants meeting the bill’s requirements no later than 90 days after the effective date of the bill. Expands the authority of a laboratory license holder to obtain adult-use and medical marijuana by adding licensed paired cultivators to the licensees from which the marijuana may be obtained.

rollCalls.title: Enact the Reagan Tokes and Patrick Heringer Act
rollCalls.summary: Requires a law enforcement agenc y to enter a warrant into the Law Enforcement Automated Database System (LEADS) and the National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database if a person escapes from detention, is on community control, and has either committed a tier one offense or is a targeted violent offender. Requires a law enforcement agency to notify the public safety answering point of the above warrant. Requires the Department of Rehabilitation and Correction (DRC) to contract with a single vendor for GPS monitoring of GPS-monitored offenders.

rollCalls.title: Revise the household sewage treatment system law
rollCalls.summary: STS inspections. Eliminates certain requirements governing the inspection of a sewage treatment system (“STS”), including mandatory initial and annual inspections for all systems. Requires the board of health to conduct an educational assessment, rather than an inspection, within 12 months after installation, at a time scheduled with the owner of the system. Maintenance program. Makes the development of a program for the administration of maintenance requirements permissive, rather than mandatory as under current law. Soil evaluations.

rollCalls.title: Regards timing of health insurer recoupment from providers
rollCalls.summary: Changes, from two years to one year, the period when:  A payment by a third-party payer to a health care provider is considered final; and  Overpayment recovery against a provider must be initiated. Prohibits a third-party payer from charging a health care provider for appealing an overcharge determination. Extends the period during which a provider may respond to an overpayment notice from 30 days to 60 days. Requires a third-party payer to give a provider a notice of overpayment electronically when using an electronic notification system agreed to by the company and provider.

rollCalls.title: Ratify the Interstate Compact for School Psychologists
rollCalls.summary: Interstate Compact for School Psychologists. Enters Ohio into the Interstate Compact for School Psychologists to improve public access to school psychological services by facilitating the interstate practice of school psychology in educational or school settings. As a member of the Compact, requires Ohio to offer equivalent licenses to school psychologists from another member state of the Compact, subject to Ohio ’s laws and rules governing school psychologists.

rollCalls.title: Enact the Enhanced Cybersecurity for SNAP Act
rollCalls.summary: Medicaid Program Integrity and Fraud Prevention Act Electronic visit verification (EVV) for in-home care services. Requires the Department of Medicaid to require each claim for a service that is subject to EVV requirements under state or federal law, including nonexempt services provided by in-home care service providers, to be supported by a validated EVV record as a condition of payment.

rollCalls.title: Make capital appropriations for the biennium ending June 30, 2028
rollCalls.summary: Capital appropriations and reappropriations. Makes capital appropriations totaling $3. 7 billion for the FY 202 7-2028 biennium, and authorizes about $3.4 billion in new debt. Aging School Accelerator Pilot Program. Establishes the Aging School Accelerator Pilot Program under which the Facilities Construction Commission (FCC) must provide classroom facilities project assistance to qualifying school districts.

rollCalls.title: CA: Require identification to vote
rollCalls.summary: Proposes an amendment to the Ohio Constitution to appear on the ballot in November 2026, to require electors to provide identification (ID) to vote. Requires an elector to show photo ID when voting in person, provided that the General Assembly may allow an exception for those with a sincere religious objection to being photographed, as under the existing statute. Defines “photo identification” to include the same documents as are currently acceptable under the Revised Code.

rollCalls.title: Revise the Ohio Uniform Commercial Code
rollCalls.summary: Establishes a new Uniform Commercial Code (UCC) Article 12 to provide rules for transactions involving certain new types of digital assets named controllable electronic records (CERs). Outlines how a person obtains control of a CER. Provides that a person with control can be anonymous, but must be positively identifiable in some manner, such as the use of a cryptographic key. Revises UCC Article 9 to facilitate the use of digital assets as collateral for loans.

rollCalls.title: Prohibit harassing or impeding an emergency service responder
rollCalls.summary: Creates new circumstances for the offense of obstructing official business. Increases the penalty for obstructing official business from a second degree misdemeanor to a first degree misdemeanor under specified circumstances involving an emergency service responder. Increases the penalty for obstructing official business from a second degree misdemeanor to a fourth degree felony if a violation creates a risk of physical harm to an emergency service responder.

rollCalls.title: Require US-produced iron, steel be used on state-funded projects
rollCalls.summary: Requires the use of iron produced in the U.S. in certain state-funded projects, in addition to the existing requirement that those projects use U.S. -produced steel, and extends relevant penalties for failure to comply. Specifies that state-funded infrastructure projects and utility infrastructure improvement projects involving water works or sewage disposal must use U.S.-produced iron and steel. Specifies that the U.S. iron and steel use requirement only applies to iron or steel products that are to be permanently incorporated in a project.

rollCalls.title: Create the Ohio International Trade Commission
rollCalls.summary: Creates the Ohio International Trade Commission. Permits the Treasurer of State to use Commission funds to purchase foreign bonds.

rollCalls.title: Limit certain public record requests; allow contractor response
rollCalls.summary: Exempts student email addresses from the Public Records Law. Permits public records keepers to initiate court proceedings to limit or deny harassing or disruptive public records requests. Permits private contractors to respond to requests for voluminous public records. Establishes an alternative fee structure that political subdivisions may adopt for public records requests.

rollCalls.title: Enact the Clinical Teaching Subsidy Reform Act
rollCalls.summary: Requires the Chancellor of Higher Education to annually distribute a clinical teaching subsidy to public medical schools to support clinical instruction and the education of physicians in Ohio. Requires the Chancellor to annually publish data including the number of full-time equivalent students enrolled in each public medical school, the performance metrics used to distribute the subsidy and the performance of each school on those metrics, and t he final subsidy allocation to each school.

rollCalls.title: Enact V.J.'s Law
rollCalls.summary: Requires health care professionals, as mandatory reporters of child abuse or neglect, to make reports to both the public children services agency (PCSA) and a peace officer, rather than to either the PCSA or a peace officer. Adds the criminal intent of acting knowingly to the prohibition on a mandatory reporter failing to immediately report known or suspected child abuse or neglect.

rollCalls.title: Regulate ticket sales
rollCalls.summary: Requires certain entertainment operators, ticket resellers, and online ticket marketplaces to conspicuously disclose various aspects regarding sales of tickets, including, for example, mandatory fees other than taxes and shipping costs. Requires ticket resellers and online ticket marketplaces to provide certain additional disclosures to assure consumers regarding ticket purchases, including, for example a 24-hour proof of purchase requirement and refund policy information.

rollCalls.title: Prohibit certain clauses from conservancy district contracts
rollCalls.summary: Prohibits a conservancy district ’s board of directors from including certain provisions, such as an indemnification clause, in a contract for the procurement of goods or services.

rollCalls.title: Regards police escorts for farm equipment, agricultural vehicles
rollCalls.summary: Exempts a farm equipment permit holder from any requirement to obtain a law enforcement escort if certain conditions are met. Requires the Director of Transportation to issue an annual permit authorizing a person to operate farm machinery or farm equipment on certain limited access highways or freeways. Authorizes a local authority to issue a similar permit if the limited access highway or freeway is under the local authority's jurisdiction.

rollCalls.title: Require the use of zero-based budgeting every ten years
rollCalls.summary: Establishes zero-based budgeting requirements for the Office of Budget and Management (OBM) Director and select state agencies beginning with the 138th General Assembly (2029-2030). Requires the Senate Finance Committee Chairperson or the House of Representatives Finance Chairperson, on a rotating basis, to select at least 1⁄3 of the state agencies to submit their estimates to OBM using zero-based budgeting. Exempts elected officials, the General Assembly, and the Supreme Court from the zero - based budgeting requirements.

rollCalls.title: Regards publicly funded child care, the Child Care Cred Program
rollCalls.summary: Revises the law governing the publicly funded child care (PFCC) program, including by eliminating the requirement that the Department of Children and Youth (DCY) calculate PFCC payments based on a child ’s enrollment, rather than a child ’s attendance, by July 9, 2028. Prohibits a child care provider participating in the PFCC program ’s automated child care system from knowingly seeking or accepting a PFCC payment for a child not in attendance with the provider, rather than for a child not enrolled with the provider as under current law.

rollCalls.title: Enact Amanda Dean's Law
rollCalls.summary: Names the act Amanda Dean’s Law. Increases the penalties for abuse of a corpse and gross abuse of a corpse. Expands the offense of gross abuse of a corpse to include dismembering, mutilating, or intentionally disfiguring a human corpse and doing so for the purpose of concealing a crime, obstructing justice, or impairing the investigation or prosecution of a criminal offense.

rollCalls.title: Regards registered veterinary technician authority
rollCalls.summary: Creates a process under which a licensed veterinarian may authorize a registered veterinary technician (RVT) to establish an assess and treat relationship on behalf of the veterinarian for certain purposes relating to a shelter dog or cat. Prohibits a person who is not an RVT from using certain titles or any other words, letters, or symbols, with the intent to represent that the person is authorized to act as an RVT.

rollCalls.title: Include maple syrup, maple product production to agriculture law
rollCalls.summary: Explicitly allows land used to produce maple syrup and maple products to qualify for the current agricultural use value (CAUV) property tax program. Expressly includes the cultivation of trees to produce maple syrup and maple products in the general statutory definition of “agriculture” and in the law s governing county and township zoning, thus expressly applying that cultivation to various laws impacted by agriculture.

rollCalls.title: Enact the Rental Home Marketplace Guarantees Act
rollCalls.summary: Prohibits a rental home marketplace guarantee from being issued or offered unless the guarantee provider has made the rental home marketplace guarantee terms available on the provider’s website and complied with the requirements of the bill. Requires all rental home marketplace guarantees to be insured under a reimbursement insurance policy. Specifies that rental home marketplace guarantees do not constitute a contract amounting to insurance and that guarantee providers are not insurance companies.

rollCalls.title: Regards SUDEP, epilepsy license designation, disability database
rollCalls.summary: Epilepsy guidance, information and education, and reporting. Requires the Director of Health, in consultation with local and national organizations that provide education or services related to epilepsy conditions to provide guidance to health care practitioners to assist them in determining when an individual is at an elevated risk for sudden unexpected death in epilepsy. Requires a health care practitioner with primary responsibility for the treatment and care of a patient who has been diagnosed with epilepsy to provide education and counseling to the patient or patient’s caregiver.

rollCalls.title: Require appointed police chief to complete officer basic training
rollCalls.summary: Generally prohibits a city, township, or village from appointing an individual as a police chief or village marshal unless the individual holds a current peace officer basic training certificate. Allows a city, township, or village to appoint an individual who does not hold a certificate as an interim police chief or village marshal for a term of not longer than six months, during which the individual must enroll in a peace officer basic training program.

rollCalls.title: Urge Congress to implement a zero-based budgeting process
Urge Congress accelerate deployment of new energy infrastructure
Urge Congress to enact the Ohio River Restoration Program Act
Regards academic intervention, math improvement and intervention
rollCalls.summary: Diagnostic assessments. Eliminates the requirement that the Department of Education and Workforce adopt one and approve five reading diagnostic assessments for grades K-3 and, instead, requires the Department to approve a list of six assessments. Adds a sixth math diagnostic assessment and provides that this assessment must be the one that scored the sixth highest in the Department’s most recent evaluation to the list of its approved math diagnostic assessments for grades K-3.

rollCalls.title: Enact the Keep Them Safe Act
rollCalls.summary: Firearms storage arrangements. Allows a person who owns a firearm or is authorized by the owner of the firearm to store the firearm with a federally licensed firearms dealer or law enforcement agency under prescribed terms. Provides immunity from civil liability for a federally licensed firearms dealer who accepts storage of a firearm under the act, unless the dealer acts with malicious purpose or intent to withhold the return of the firearm without legal cause.

rollCalls.title: Designate Congressman David Hobson Memorial Highway
rollCalls.summary: Designates multiple highways, an interchange, bridge, and overpass. Creates multiple new specialty license plates.

rollCalls.title: Enact the Enhanced Cybersecurity for SNAP Act of 2025
rollCalls.summary: Requires the Ohio Department of Job and Family Services (ODJFS) to replace all existing electronic benefit transfer cards used to provide benefits for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) with cards that are chip-enabled. Requires the ODJFS Director to adopt rules regarding cybersecurity and digital service related to SNAP electronic benefit transfer cards and mobile payments. Requires the Director to ensure that the ODJFS website contains a mechanism for SNAP benefit recipients to report fraud.

rollCalls.title: Establish process to regulate carbon capture, storage technology
rollCalls.summary: Authority to regulate carbon sequestration. Declares that the regulation of carbon dioxide sequestration activities is a matter of general statewide interest that requires uniform statewide regulation. Generally, grants the Division of Oil and Gas Resources Management within the Ohio Department of Natural Resources (ODNR) sole and exclusive authority to regulate carbon sequestration.

rollCalls.title: Allow surviving spouse to retain Purple Heart license plate
rollCalls.summary: Allows certain surviving spouses of a Purple Heart recipient to retain or obtain the “Purple Heart” license plate.

rollCalls.title: Increase the penalties for voyeurism
rollCalls.summary: Increases the penalty for voyeurism regarding the viewing of another person’s private area to a fifth degree felony and increases the penalty to a fourth degree felony if the offender has previously been convicted of or pleaded guilty to a violation of the offense. Increases the penalty for voyeurism regarding viewing the body or undergarments of another to a fifth degree felony and increases the penalty to a fourth degree felony if the offender has previously been convicted of or pleaded guilty to a violation of the offense.

rollCalls.title: Regards the one-year limitations period for libel or slander
rollCalls.summary: Specifies when a cause of action for libel or slander begins. Increases the limitations period from one year to four years for libel or slander.

rollCalls.title: Enact the Future Educators Support Act
rollCalls.summary: Student teacher stipend and tuition rate. Allows a public school to pay a student teacher a stipend in an amount determined by the school. Authorizes a state institution of higher education to establish a lower differential tuition rate, which may include a waiver of general or instructional fees, for an individual enrolled in a teacher preparation program for the period during which the individual is working as a student teacher or participating in any other teacher preparation program field experience. List of in-demand teaching jobs.

rollCalls.title: Require 7 year mandatory minimum prison term for forcible rape
rollCalls.summary: Imposes a minimum mandatory prison term on an offen der who engages in sexual conduct with another when the offender purposely compels the other person to submit by force or threat of force. Requires the minimum mandatory prison term to be at least seven years, but allows the minimum mandatory prison term to be 7, 8, 9, 10, or 11 years. Expands the definition of “sexual conduct ” to include anilingus between persons regardless of sex.

rollCalls.title: Regards embalmers, funeral directors, and crematories
rollCalls.summary: Specifies that a transportation protection agreement that primarily provides or arranges for services that are related to transporting human remains or cremated remains or preparing such remains for transport is not a preneed funeral contract.

rollCalls.title: Regards paid family leave insurance
rollCalls.summary: Imposes requirements on policies of paid family leave insurance. Requires a policy of paid family leave insurance to lay out all details and requirements with regard to coverage for each form of family leave covered under the policy. Requires policies of paid family leave insurance that impose waiting periods to set forth the terms and conditions of the waiting period. Specifies that the length of family leave benefits provided in a policy of paid family leave insurance cannot be less than two weeks during a period of 52 consecutive calendar weeks.

rollCalls.title: Create defense to nuisance claims re: racing facilities
rollCalls.summary: Creates a complete defense to a civil action for nuisances involving a racing facility and racetrack arising on or after the bill’s effective date if certain conditions are met. Prohibits a county or township from adopting or enforcing a resolution that conflicts with the bill. Provides that the bill is not to be construed to exempt a racing facility and racetrack from compliance with state or federal environmental laws or health and safety regulations, or from a claim based on physical damage or personal injury.

rollCalls.title: Designate Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) Month
Verify veteran status of imprisoned individuals
rollCalls.summary: Requires incarcerating institutions to investigate and verify the veteran status of individuals imprisoned or charged with a criminal offense punishable by incarceration. Specifies that a sheriff’s jail register must include a prisoner’s veteran status. Specifies that outreach and coordination programs established by a county veterans service commission may provide financial assistance to veterans treatment courts, and training and equipment for incarcerating institutions necessary to comply with the act’s requirements.

rollCalls.title: Revise the law governing oil and gas wells
rollCalls.summary: Oil and Gas Well Fund. Provides protections against executive branch raids of the Oil and Gas Well Fund. Specifies that the Division of Oil and Gas Resources Management, on behalf of the state, owns the right to carbon credits for any orphaned well plugged using state or federal money. Allows the Chief of the Division to enter into agreements to obtain or to sell carbon credits and directs any proceeds from the sale of carbon credits to the Oil and Gas Well Fund. ODNR authority to regulate interstate wells.

rollCalls.title: Require construction contracts note variation from standard form
rollCalls.summary: Requires that when a public construction contract uses an industry standard form, any changes to the standard terms must be indicated by marking up the contract, or the changes are not valid and the contract defaults to the industry standard.

rollCalls.title: Regards professional employer organizations and Unemployment Law
rollCalls.summary: Allows a professional employer organization (PEO), alternate employer organization (AEO), or PEO reporting entit y to elect to report shared employees of a client employer under the account and experience rate of the PEO, AEO, or PEO reporting entity for purposes of reporting that information under the Unemployment Compensation Law, rather than using a separate, unique subaccount, as required under former law.

rollCalls.title: Require electronic recordings of all parole board hearings
rollCalls.summary: Requires the Chief of the Adult Parole Authority to adopt rules requiring that electronic recordings be made of Parole Board hearings. Makes electronic recordings of full Parole Board hearings public records. Clarifies that electronic recordings of institutional Parole Board release consideration hearings, revocation hearings, post-release control revocation hearings, and specified Parole Board hearings are not public records.

rollCalls.title: Regards Ohio State, Local Government Expenditure Databases
rollCalls.summary: Establishes the Ohio Local Government Expenditure Database and requires certain political subdivisions to participate. Requires state retirement systems to participate in the Ohio State Government Expenditure Database. Requires both systems to include revenue data.

rollCalls.title: Modify trust and probate laws
rollCalls.summary: Ohio Trust Protector and Directed Trust Act. Enacts the Ohio Trust Protector and Directed Trust Act (OTPDTA). Establishes eligibility requirements to serve as a protector, and establishes the powers, authority, and duties attributable to protectors. Prohibits concurrent service as trustee and protector of the same trust. Establishes procedures for the designation, compensation, resignation, removal, and vacancies of protectors. Requires beneficiaries of a trust to be notified in advance of any change in the method or rate of the trust protector’s compensation.

rollCalls.title: Create jury tampering offense; revise court intimidation offenses
rollCalls.summary: Creates the offense of “jury tampering.”. Expands the offense of “intimidation of an attorney, victim, or witness” to include a public servant.

rollCalls.title: Enact the Grand Jury Privacy and Protection Act
rollCalls.summary: Exempts from disclosure under Public Records Law, the name and address of a grand juror and the signature of a grand-jury foreperson. Names the bill the “Grand Jury Privacy and Protection Act.”.

rollCalls.title: Align and modernize fingerprinting and disposition reporting
rollCalls.summary: Collection of identifying information. Clarifies when fingerprints and other identifying information must be collected upon arrest or at other stages of the criminal justice process. Requires electronic submission of identifying information and case summaries in the form and manner prescribed by the Superintendent of the Bureau of Criminal Identification and Investigation (BCI). Fingerprint and case status communication. Clarifies procedures and timing for fingerprinting requirement s, and responsibility for transmission to BCI. Sealing and expungement.

rollCalls.title: Create the Ohio, The Heart of It All Pass program
rollCalls.summary: Creates the Ohio, The Heart of It All pass program in the Department of Development (DEV), to be administered by TourismOhio, the purpose of which is to promote Ohio ’s artistic, cultural, historical, educational, recreational, film, and museum attractions. Provides a free pass, for 2026, to all Ohio residents who apply for it, and for 2027 and beyond permits any person to purchase a pass (with a discount for Ohio residents). Permits TourismOhio to adopt rules to implement the program.

rollCalls.title: Regulate the ownership of electric vehicle charging stations
rollCalls.summary: Adds definitions for “electric vehicle ” and “electric vehicle charging station ” to Ohio ’s Competitive Retail Electric Services (CRES) laws. Declares electric vehicle charging station s are a CRES that consumers may obtain from any supplier, subject to Ohio’s CRES laws. Amends provisions of recently enacted S.B. 103 of the 136th General Assembly to ensure that water service line replacement costs and water service line replacement reimbursement amounts are included in the property valuation calculation of a utility that chooses to file for a forecasted test period.

rollCalls.title: Require ODNR discount program for veterans, service members
rollCalls.summary: Requires the ODNR Chief of the Division of Parks and Watercraft to establish a discount program for veterans and service members for state park services and rentals.

rollCalls.title: Require certain facilities assist inmates in obtaining ID cards
rollCalls.summary: Expands a program through which certain prison inmates are provided assistance in obtaining a state identification card (“ID card”) prior to their release from confinement. Specifically, adds inmates completing programming at a community-based correctional facility and program, a district community-based correctional facility and program, or a halfway house to the ID card program.

rollCalls.title: Regulate practice of surgical assistants, surgical technologists
rollCalls.summary: Prohibits a hospital or ambulatory surgical facility from employing an individual as a surgical assistant or surgical technologist unless the individual is certified as an assistant or technologist or has practiced as one during any part of the six-month period immediately preceding the bill’s effective date.

rollCalls.title: Regards student use of a nasal epinephrine delivery device
rollCalls.summary: Permits public and private schools and camps to procure epinephrine nasal sprays and other epinephrine devices or products approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for use in emergency situations in the same capacity as epinephrine autoinjectors. Permits students to possess and use such a device or product in public and private schools and camps. Requires the Ohio State Board of Pharmacy to adopt rules designating devices or other products that are FDA-approved for administering a premeasured dose of epinephrine that may be used in schools and camps.

rollCalls.title: Create Higher Ed Evidence-Based Innovation Fund, Grant Program
rollCalls.summary: Creates the Higher Education Evidence-based Innovation Fund and Grant Program. Requires the Chancellor of Higher Education to award competitive grants from the fund to state institutions of higher education to support student success programs that use evidence-based reforms or practices.

rollCalls.title: Establish a universal regulatory sandbox program
rollCalls.summary: Creates the Universal Regulatory Sandbox Program (referred to in this analysis as the “sandbox program”). Establishes the Universal Regulatory Sandbox Program Advisory Committee and a regulatory relief division, within the Governor ’s Common Sense Initiative (CSI) office, to administer the sandbox program. Provides guidelines and required materials for the sandbox program application. Describes the evaluation process of applicants to the sandbox program. Establishes guidelines on the limits of an approved participant ’s demonstration and offering.

rollCalls.title: Enact Aspen Runnels' Law
rollCalls.summary: Increases the penalties for vehicular manslaughter and vehicular assault that are the proximate result of speeding or the commission of a traffic offense in an active school zone. Authorizes a court to double the fine for certain traffic offenses that occur in a school- adjacent sector. Authorizes a court to require an offender who committed vehicular homicide or assault in an active school zone to complete a remedial driving course prior to reinstating that offender’s driver’s license.

rollCalls.title: Enact the Finding and Identifying with NamUs Data (FIND) Act
rollCalls.summary: Names the act Andy Chapman’s Act. Requires law enforcement who takes a report of a missing child to assess if the child may be a high-risk missing child. Requires law enforcement, who has reason to believe a child or person is a high-risk missing child or person, to contact the appropriate county prosecutor who is required to determine if the child or person is a high-risk missing child or person.

rollCalls.title: Regards health insurance, Medicaid prior authorization
rollCalls.summary: Requires health insuring corporations, sickness and accident insurers, public employee benefit plans, (collectively, “health insurers”) and the Department of Medicaid (ODM) to honor a prior authorization approval if a provider prescribes a change in dosage of the approved drug. Requires that the specialty and relevant qualifications of the clinical peer, who is required by continuing law to review prior authorization appeals, to be identified. Prohibits health insurers and ODM from charging a fee for appealing an adverse prior authorization determination.

rollCalls.title: Enact the Indecent Exposure Modernization Act
rollCalls.summary: Creates the offense of “unlawful adult cabaret performance” that prohibits a person, with knowledge of its character and content, from recklessly engaging in an adult cabaret performance in a location other than an adult cabaret. Provides that the penalty for “unlawful adult cabaret performance ” is a first degree misdemeanor or a fourth or fifth degree felony depending on the circumstances of the offense. Names the act the “Indecent Exposure Modernization Act.”.

rollCalls.title: Modify offenses of burglary, breaking and entering, and trespass
rollCalls.summary: Creates new “aggravated burglary,” “burglary,” and “trespass in a habitation where a person is present or likely to be present” offenses that are the same as the current offenses except that the new offenses do not require that the offender commit the offense by “force, stealth, or deception” and require the offender to commit the offense with a mental state of “knowingly.”. Specifies that the new offenses and the current offenses are allied offenses of similar import. Establishes penalties for the new offenses and generally increases penalties for the current offenses.

rollCalls.title: Enact SHE WINS Act
rollCalls.summary: Permits an elective abortion to be performed or induced only if a physician meets with the woman at least 24 hours before the abortion to provide specified information and document the woman’s informed consent, except in the case of a medical emergency. Prohibits payment from being required for any elective abortion-related service until the bill’s informed consent requirements are met. Authorizes civil liability, including damages and attorney’s fees, and professional discipline against a physician who fails to satisfy the bill ’s abortion informed consent requirements.

rollCalls.title: Enact the Larry Henderson Act
rollCalls.summary: Modifies the class of victims for aggravated murder to include peace officers, corrections officers, and prosecutors. Modifies the class of victims for a specification of aggravating circumstances to include peace officers, corrections officers, and prosecutors. Includes an additional class of victims for a specification of aggravating circumstances to include first responders and military members.

rollCalls.title: Regards excused school absences for 4-H and FFA programs
rollCalls.summary: Requires a school district to count a student who participates in a district-approved school-sponsored or workforce preparation activity during school hours as being present at school.

rollCalls.title: Regards entities providing behind-the-meter utility services
Establish licensing process, contract requirements for PBMs
rollCalls.summary: PBM licensure. Establishes a stand-alone licensing process for pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) beginning July 1, 2027, and on that date, excludes PBMs from regulation under the third-party administrator (TPA) licensure law. Prohibits a person from soliciting a health plan sponsor or providing pharmacy benefit management services in Ohio without a PBM license, and makes it a fourth degree misdemeanor for a person to knowingly do so. Prescribes eligibility criteria for a PBM license depending on if the applicant is an individual, a business entity, or a nonresident licensed in another state.

rollCalls.title: Designate Patrolman Earl W. Casterline Memorial Highway
Exempt military-certified child care providers from licensure
rollCalls.summary: Exempts family child care providers certified by the U.S. armed forces from the law governing the regulation of child care providers, including the requirement that certain family child care homes be licensed by the Department of Children and Youth.

rollCalls.title: Revise list of vehicles that can commit vehicular homicide
rollCalls.summary: Regarding vehicles that can be used to commit vehicular homicide or assault, adds the following vehicles:  Under-speed vehicles (e.g., golf cart);  Motorized bicycles or mopeds;  Motor-driven cycles or motor scooters; and  All-purpose vehicles.

rollCalls.title: Require tick-related disease reporting to Department of Health
rollCalls.summary: Revises the law requiring health-related entities and individuals, including boards of health and health care providers, to promptly report to the Department of Health the existence of certain diseases and conditions, including by requiring reports of alpha-gal syndrome.

rollCalls.title: Create the Data Center Study Commission
rollCalls.summary: Data center electric service. Requires, as of the bill ’s effective date, each new data center in Ohio with an aggregate monthly maximum demand of greater than 250 megawatts to be supplied with all of its electricity using any or all of the following sources that must offset any consumption from the electrical grid by the data center:  One or more electric generating facilities constructed to supply electricity to the data center (with nameplate capacity determined by multiplying the facility ’s nameplate capacity by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission reliability factor);  One or more…

rollCalls.title: Make capital reappropriations for biennium ending June 30, 2028
rollCalls.summary: Makes capital reappropriations for the biennium ending June 30, 2028 (FYs 2027 and 2028) and other appropriations. Makes various supplemental appropriations and earmarks.

rollCalls.title: Enact the Innocence Act
rollCalls.summary: Names specific provisions of the bill the “Innocence Act.”. Requires an organization that sells, delivers, furnishes, disseminates, provides, exhibits, or presents any material or performance that is obscene or harmful to juveniles ensure that a geolocation check is performed. Requires an organization to submit an affidavit to the Attorney General stating that the organization complied with the age verification requirements. Requires the Attorney General to adopt rules specifying the information that organizations must include in the affidavit.

rollCalls.title: Regards unpaid water, sewer, and trash charges at rented property
rollCalls.summary: Prohibits the appropriate municipal authority from certifying a lien to the county auditor for unpaid village water, city water, or municipal sewerage service amounts, and prohibits the county auditor from placing such a lien against a property, if either of the following apply:  The unpaid amounts have arisen pursuant to a service contract made with a tenant;  The property served by the connection is not occupied by the property owner.

rollCalls.title: Establish the Foster-to-College Scholarship Program
rollCalls.summary: Requires the Director of Education and Workforce, in collaboration with specified other state agency leaders, to encourage the sharing of best practices to support students placed in foster care. Requires each public school to designate a local foster care education liaison to support students in foster care. Requires each public school, for each school building it operates, to designate a building staff member as the foster family navigator to serve as the primary point of contact to support students placed in foster care that attend that school.

rollCalls.title: Establish the Ohio Defense Commission
rollCalls.summary: Establishes the Ohio Defense and Space Advisory Commission. Establishes the Defense and Aerospace Industry Expansion Program under which the Department of Development may make grants to support economic development related to the defense industry. Requires any entity that receives a grant under the program undergo an audit of the project administration. Makes an appropriation.

rollCalls.title: Designate Detective Rex Emrick Memorial Highway
Enact the Healthy Cardiac Monitoring Act
rollCalls.summary: Prohibits a student or youth athlete from being allowed to participate in an athletic activity unless the athlete has a physical examination performed by a physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant, and the health care provider completes a preparticipation physical evaluation form.

rollCalls.title: Prohibit a person from receiving proceeds of prostitution
rollCalls.summary: Creates the offense of receiving proceeds of prostitution. Includes receiving proceeds of prostitution as a corrupt activity, subject to the Corrupt Activities Law.

rollCalls.title: Establish Frontier Technologies and Quantum Computing Commission
rollCalls.summary: Establishes the Frontier Technologies and Quantum Commission, as a temporary Commission, to study the rapid development of frontier technologies with significant economic, ethical, and security implications for Ohio. Requires the Commission to prepare and deliver a report of its findings and recommendations to the General Assembly not later than December 31, 2026. Requires the Legislative Service Commission, upon request, to provide support to the Commission.

rollCalls.title: Designate Abbey Gate Remembrance Day
Modify excavation requirements
rollCalls.summary: One call utility protection service. Requires protection services to create and maintain databases to collect and track underground facility damage notifications made in accordance with the reporting duties of excavators, and provide certain information for the purpose of improving excavation safety, damage prevention education, and transparency.

rollCalls.title: Create the small defense business linked deposit program
rollCalls.summary: Creates the Small Defense Business Linked Deposit Program for the purpose of lending money to eligible small defense businesses, including their subcontractors, at a rate below the present borrowing rate. Adds the Small Defense Business Linked Deposit Program to the administrative requirements in the statutes also governing the continuing Adoption Linked Deposit Program, Agricultural Linked Deposit Program, Small Business Linked Deposit Program, and Home Improvement Linked Deposit Program.

rollCalls.title: Remove residency requirements for certain city director positions
rollCalls.summary: Removes residency requirements for the city director of public services and the city director of public safety.

rollCalls.title: Regards physician supervision of imaging contrast administration
rollCalls.summary: Administration of contrast – physician supervision. Revises the law authorizing a radiologist assistant to administer contrast media under the on-site supervision of a physician who is a radiologist, by also permitting the radiologist assistant to do so under the radiologist’s remote supervision. Authorizes a registered nurse, radiographer, radiation therapy technologist, and nuclear medicine technologist to administer contrast under the direct or general supervision of a physician.

rollCalls.title: Designate a school JROTC program as a career-technical ed program
rollCalls.summary: Permits a school district that offers a Junior Reserve Officer Training Corps (JROTC) or National Defense Cadet Corps (NDCC) program to designate that program as part of the district’s career-technical education (CTE) program. Requires the Department of Education and Workforce to include in the calculation of a school district’s CTE funding any JROTC or NDCC program a district designates as part of its CTE program.

rollCalls.title: Regards voter approval of municipal income tax reciprocity credit
rollCalls.summary: Requires voter approval to decrease or repeal an existing municipal income tax reciprocity credit. Allows a voter initiative to authorize or increase a reciprocity credit. Requires the Department of Taxation to conduct a study on municipal income taxes, with a variety of stakeholders, and issue a report to the General Assembly.

rollCalls.title: Regards custody of children who cannot be released to a parent
rollCalls.summary: Requires a court officer or law enforcement officer who takes custody of a child in specified circumstances to immediately notify the public children services agency (PCSA) of the county in which the child is taken into custody if the child cannot be released to a parent, guardian, or custodian.

rollCalls.title: Designate Deputy Daniel "Weston" Sherrer Memorial Highway
Create recovery housing residences certificate of need program
rollCalls.summary: Recovery housing residences State certification. Converts the program used by the Department of Behavioral Health to monitor recovery housing residences into a state certification program, thereby eliminating the option of relying solely on accrediting organizations. Permits the converted program to include acceptance of accreditation in a manner similar to the monitoring program, but limits the purpose of accepting accreditation to the portion of the state certification program that involves determining whether state standards have been satisfied.

rollCalls.title: Regards recording of certain real property documents
rollCalls.summary: Liens. Requires a lien creditor to provide the last known address of a lien debtor when filing a lien relating to unpaid child support and personal property taxes. Requires a lien creditor to provide the name of the lien debtor and last known address when filing a lien relating to workers compensation, unemployment compensation, sales taxes, income taxes, or severance taxes. Recording of a memorandum of trust. Requires a memorandum of trust or other qualifying instrument to be “of record” when an interest in real property is conveyed by the trustee of a disclosed trust.

rollCalls.title: Require hospitals to provide overdose reversal drugs
rollCalls.summary: Generally requires a hospital to provide an overdose reversal drug to a patient at the time of the patient ’s discharge, if the patient presented to the hospital ’s emergency department with symptoms of opioid use disorder or overdose. Requires the Department of Behavioral Health to provide overdose reversal drugs to hospitals, subject to available funds. Permits a hospital to seek insurance or Medicaid reimbursement for overdose reversal drug costs, but only if the drugs were provided to patients from a supply purchased by the hospital.

rollCalls.title: Designate Cardiovascular Health Awareness Day
Prohibit use of ranked choice voting; withhold funding for use
rollCalls.summary: Ranked choice voting. Prohibits any election from being conducted in Ohio using ranked choice voting, also known as instant runoff voting. Allows a county or municipal corporation to use its home rule powers under the Ohio Constitution to adopt a ranked choice voting system, but financially penalizes a local government that does so. Makes a county or municipal corporation that approves the use of ranked choice voting via a resolution or ordinance ineligible to receive distributions from the Local Government Fund until it rescinds the resolution or ordinance.

rollCalls.title: Incorporate Internal Revenue Code changes into Ohio law
rollCalls.summary: Incorporates changes to federal tax law taking effect since March 7, 202 5, into Ohio income tax law. Declares an emergency.

rollCalls.title: Delay offender financial sanctions until 180 days after release
rollCalls.summary: Prohibits a court from requiring an offender to pay any outstanding court-assessed fines, fees, financial sanctions, or costs arising from a criminal proceeding during either of the following periods, whichever is later:  The 180 days following the offender’s release from a prison sentence of one year or more;  The 180 days following the offender’s completion of a transitional control period. States that delaying the payment of fines, fees, financial sanctions, or costs does not apply to restitution owed to a victim.

rollCalls.title: Regards the Classic Learning Test entrance exam
rollCalls.summary: Eliminates the requirement that the Department of Education and Workforce and the Chancellor of Higher Education jointly select the assessments from which schools must choose for the College and Work Ready Assessment System. Instead, p ermits public and chartered nonpublic schools to select the nationally standardized assessment, which may be the ACT, SAT, Classic Learning Test, or any other valid, reliable, nationally norm-referenced exam used for college admission.

rollCalls.title: Designate PFC Thomas "Tommy" Pizzino Memorial Highway
Waive ID, birth certificate fees for homeless individuals
rollCalls.summary: Absent voting by mail. Would have required an elector to provide photo identification ( ID) to vote by mail beginning with the November 2027, general election. Would have exempted certain electors from that requirement and provided alternative ID procedures for them. Would have allowed an elector to fulfill the photo ID requirement by providing it either when applying for ballots or when returning voted ballots to the board. Would have permitted an elector to show photo ID at the board’s office instead of making a copy.

rollCalls.title: Convene in joint session of Senate and House
Regards the timeline for restoring competency in criminal cases
rollCalls.summary: Increases in some instances, the time during which a criminal defendant may be held, prior to trial, for purposes of restoring the defendant’s competency. Tolls or restarts the time limit for restoration of competency under certain circumstances. Applies retroactively to any criminal defendant found incompetent to stand trial prior to February 20, 2026, and whose restoration to competency is ongoing or whose case remains pending. Declares an emergency.

rollCalls.title: Incorporate Internal Revenue Code changes into Ohio law
rollCalls.summary: Incorporates changes to federal tax law taking effect since March 7, 202 5, into Ohio income tax law. Declares an emergency.

rollCalls.title: Restrict sex offender from residing, loitering near victim’s home
rollCalls.summary: Restrictions under Ohio’s SORN Laws. Prohibits a sex offender or child-victim offender from knowingly establishing a residence or occupying a residential premises within 2,000 feet of the residential premises of the victim of the sexually oriented offense or child-victim oriented offense committed by the offender. Prohibits a sex offender or child-victim offender from knowingly loitering within 1,000 feet of the residential premises of the victim of the sexually oriented offense or child-victim oriented offense committed by the offender.

rollCalls.title: Revise non-recourse litigation funding agreement regulations
rollCalls.summary: Overview. Repeals the law governing nonrecourse civil litigation advance contract s and replaces it with two subsets of regulations: one for commercial litigation financing agreements (“commercial agreements ”) and another for consumer legal funding agreements (“consumer agreements”). Contract requirements. Retains the majority of the contract-related requirements under former law, but limits application of those requirements to consumer agreements, i.e., contracts with an individual that resides in Ohio for less than $400,000.

rollCalls.title: Regards age requirements for kindergarten admission
rollCalls.summary: Requires public schools to admit to kindergarten any child who will be five years old or, if the child has not completed first grade, six years old, by the first day of instruction of the school year of admittance. Requires the Department of Education and Workforce to address a scoring error on the 2024-2025 biology end-of-course exam, including by increasing the scores of students negatively affected by it.

rollCalls.title: Limit ability to reallocate certain school property tax millage
rollCalls.summary: Requires that current expense fixed-sum levies be included in the calculation of a school district’s 20-mill floor or a joint vocational school district ’s 2-mill floor for property tax purposes, as follows:  Includes existing emergency and substitute levies in the first tax year, beginning in tax year 2026, in which a county in which the district has territory undergoes a reappraisal or triennial update.  Includes existing growth and conversion levies and fixed-sum property taxes levied with a school district income tax beginning in tax year 2026.

rollCalls.title: Authorize home kitchen registration for sale of certain foods
rollCalls.summary: Authorizes the production and sale of homemade foods under a microenterprise home kitchen operation registration. Establishes requirements governing a microenterprise home kitchen operation for all of the following:  Operation;  Food safety; and  Sales and delivery. Requires the Department of Agriculture (ODA) Director or the Director ’s designee to inspect the home kitchen of every operation. Codifies custom meat processing standards that apply to game animals, migratory waterfowl, and game birds.

rollCalls.title: Prescribe limitations on intercollegiate athlete contracts
rollCalls.summary: Contracts with intercollegiate athletes. Prohibits any person from entering into a name, image, or likeness (NIL) contract with an intercollegiate athlete if the contract remains in effect or requires the athlete to provide future compensation or rights associated with the use of the athlete’s NIL after the athlete’s intercollegiate athletic eligibility ends.

rollCalls.title: Prescribe limitations on intercollegiate athlete contracts
rollCalls.summary: Contracts with intercollegiate athletes. Prohibits any person from entering into a name, image, or likeness (NIL) contract with an intercollegiate athlete if the contract remains in effect or requires the athlete to provide future compensation or rights associated with the use of the athlete’s NIL after the athlete’s intercollegiate athletic eligibility ends.

rollCalls.title: Regards school district property taxes, school funding formula
rollCalls.summary: Tax credit for property in school districts on 20-mill floor. Authorizes a property tax credit for the owners of property located in a school district on the 20-mill floor property tax floor, with the goal of limiting a district’s total property tax revenue growth from the floor to the rate of inflation. Applies to all eligible property in the state beginning in tax year 2025.

rollCalls.title: Revise dog law, including dangerous and vicious dogs
rollCalls.summary: Nuisance, dangerous, and vicious dog acts. Redefines what constitutes a nuisance, dangerous, and vicious dog. Penalties for dog attacks. Imposes criminal penalties on a dog owner or an animal shelter for dogs if:  The dog owner negligently fails to keep their dog from committing, without provocation, a “nuisance dog act,” “dangerous dog act,” or “vicious dog act,” including in circumstances in which the dog has not previously engaged in such an act;  The animal shelter for dogs recklessly fails to keep the dog from committing such acts.

rollCalls.title: Regards funds provided by county for Memorial Day expenses
rollCalls.summary: Increases the amount a county may provide to military and veterans organizations for Memorial Day expenses. Increases from $100 to $200 the amount a county may appropriate to a civic organization for Memorial Day expenses.

rollCalls.title: Establish community energy program and pilot program
rollCalls.summary: Community energy facilities. Amends state competitive retail electric service ( CRES) policy to add provisions relating to community energy facilities and the establishment of the Community Energy Pilot Program. Defines “community energy facility” (CEF) as a single facility that generates electricity by means of a solar photovoltaic device or uses as its fuel either solar, wind, biomass, landfill gas, or hydroelectric power, or uses a microturbine, natural gas-fired generator, energy storage system, or a fuel cell and meets certain other requirements.

rollCalls.title: Regards budget commissions, property tax, and certain funds
rollCalls.summary: County budget commissions. Limits a requirement that county budget commissions (CBCs) approve all properly authorized voted property tax levies without modification to only the first year of a levy’s collection. Authorizes CBCs to reduce property tax levies, provided they are not otherwise required to approve them without modification, to avoid unnecessary or excessive collections.

rollCalls.title: Enact the Patient Protection Act
rollCalls.summary: Charges the Director of Health with determining if a prescription drug causes severe adverse effects in greater than 5% of the drug’s users and requires the Director to do so in consultation with the Superintendent of Insurance and Executive Directors of the State Board of Pharmacy and State Medical Board. Defines a severe adverse effect to mean any of the following: death, infection or hemorrhaging requiring hospitalization, organ failure, or sepsis.

rollCalls.title: Regards county budget commissions, property and sales tax, funds
rollCalls.summary: Requires each county budget commission (CBC), in the county ’s reappraisal or update year, to adjust the rate of each inside millage levy to limit any increase in its revenue to the GDP deflator growth over the three preceding years. Allows a subdivision to request that the CBC increase the levy rate to collect the same amount as the previous year if the subdivision’s inside millage collections would not increase in a reappraisal year.

rollCalls.title: Enact Andy's Law
rollCalls.summary: Andy’s Law. Names the act Andy’s Law. Aggravated murder. Expands the offense of aggravated murder to prohibit causing the death of specific persons interacting with a correctional department, institution, or facility. Expands the offense of aggravated murder to prohibit causing the death of specific persons when it is the offender’s specific purpose to kill those persons.

rollCalls.title: Require certain facilities assist inmates in obtaining ID cards
rollCalls.summary: Expands a program through which certain prison inmates are provided assistance in obtaining a state identification card (“ID card”) prior to their release from confinement. Specifically, adds inmates completing programming at a community-based correctional facility and program, a district community-based correctional facility and program, or a halfway house to the ID card program.

rollCalls.title: Expand allowable uses of profits from jail commissary funds
rollCalls.summary: Expands the allowable uses of jail commissary funds profits. Stipulates that any record pertaining to the use of a jail commissary fund is a public record subject to disclosure under the Public Records Law.

rollCalls.title: Regards the operation of public schools and the DEW
rollCalls.summary: State Board of Education. Increases the number of appointed State Board of Education members from five to seven. Requires the State Board, in some circumstances, to add additional grade levels to alternative resident educator license holders ’ licenses as requested by the educator ’s employing school district. Requires the State Board to automatically revoke or deny the renewal of any license issued to an individual who pleads guilty to, is found guilty of, or is convicted of domestic violence, strangulation, or grooming.

rollCalls.title: Authorize online raffles under the Charitable Gaming Law
rollCalls.summary: Traditional vs. online raffles. Divides raffles into two categories: a “traditional raffle” that uses only physical tickets and an “online raffle ” that uses an online raffle platform and electronic representations of tickets. Traditional raffles. Clarifies that an entity that conducts a traditional raffle may accept electronic payments for tickets and may sell tickets over the internet or by other remote means, so long as certain requirements are met. Sets out requirements for prize drawings and types of prizes.

rollCalls.title: Enact the Baby Olivia Act
rollCalls.summary: Requires each public school to provide human growth and development instruction in its curriculum for grades 5-12, which must include a high-definition ultrasound video and the “Meet Baby Olivia ” video produced by Live Action, or its successor entity, or a substantially similar video. Prohibits the Department of Education and Workforce from adopting a model curriculum in human growth and development that conflicts with the bill’s requirements. Requires the Department to establish and publicize a list of instructional materials in human growth and development compliant with the bill.

rollCalls.title: Enact the Charlie Kirk American Heritage Act
rollCalls.summary: Declares the General Assembly’s findings that the “teaching of the historical, positive impact of religion on American history is consistent with the First Amendment ” and “imperative to reducing ignorance of American history, hate, and violence within our society.”. Permits teachers in public schools and instructors at state institutions of higher education, when providing instruction on American history, to also provide instruction on the positive impacts of religion on American history. Entitles the bill the “Charlie Kirk American Heritage Act.”.

rollCalls.title: Prohibit interfering with motor vehicle-related arrests
rollCalls.summary: Expands the offense of interfering with an officer who is arresting an offender for a violation of a criminal traffic or vehicle equipment law. Increases the penalty for this offense from a minor misdemeanor to a second degree misdemeanor. Creates a new offense that generally prohibits a vehicle operator or passenger from refusing to disclose the person’s name, address, or birthdate when requested by a peace officer who reasonably suspects that the person has committed a violation of certain offenses related to the laws governing motor vehicles and other modes of transit.

rollCalls.title: Prohibit specified actions with intent to steal a motor vehicle
rollCalls.summary: Gas and diesel fuel tax. Reduces the tax on gasoline and diesel fuel for a period of three months, from 38.5 ¢ per gallon for gasoline and 47¢ per gallon for diesel to 0.01¢ per gallon for either. Prohibits a licensed retail dealer or licensed motor fuel dealer from selling motor fuel during the temporary reduction period without passing the full benefit of the reduced tax onto the consumer or other purchaser. Provides that violation of the prohibition may be considered in any licensing determination made by the Tax Commissioner and referred to the Attorney General (AG).

rollCalls.title: Revise and streamline the state’s occupational regulations
rollCalls.summary: This analysis is arranged by the general provisions affecting occupational review followed by the state agencies subject to review this biennium.

rollCalls.title: Regards drug trafficking, human trafficking, and fentanyl
rollCalls.summary: Drug offense changes. Increases the penalties and changes the quantities required for trafficking cocaine, fentanyl-related compounds, heroin, and methamphetamine. Removes the knowledge requirement for possession of a fentanyl-related compound when the other drug involved is marihuana and when the other drug is a Schedule III, IV, or V controlled substance that is not a fentanyl-related compound. Requires that all death certificates include a space to indicate whether the cause of death was due to fentanyl poisoning. Fentanyl abuse prevention instruction and awareness.

rollCalls.title: Allow alternative rate plans for certain natural gas companies
rollCalls.summary: Forecasted test periods and property valuation. Allows a natural gas, water-works, and sewage disposal system company (“utility company”) to propose a forecasted test period, consisting of three consecutive 12-month periods, in the same manner as an electric light company (ELC) under continuing law, which includes the following:  Being subject to the same property valuation and reporting requirements as ELCs;  Providing any financial information from the utility company ’s full books, which the Public Utilities Commission (PUCO) must protect from disclosure of trade secrets or proprietary…

rollCalls.title: Designate 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion Day
Authorize conveyance of state-owned land.
rollCalls.summary: Authorizes 14 transactions for the sale or transfer of state-owned land or the granting of easements on state-owned land.

rollCalls.title: Revise deadline to return absent voter ballots
rollCalls.summary: Absentee ballot deadline. Requires all regular absentee ballots that are returned by mail to be delivered to the appropriate board of elections by the close of the polls (7:30 p.m.) on Election Day to be counted, eliminating a four-day grace period for those ballots under prior law. Electors’ U.S. citizenship. Changes the process the Secretary of State (SOS) must use to review the Statewide Voter Registration Database to identify non-U.S. citizens.

rollCalls.title: Revise medical and adult-use marijuana laws; levy marijuana taxes
rollCalls.summary: Overview. Repeals the Cannabis Control Law and combines regulations concerning the cultivation, processing, dispensing, use, and home grow of adult-use and medical marijuana into one chapter, referred to in this analysis as the Marijuana Control Law. Condenses the operations of the Division of Cannabis Control ( DCC) and the Division of Marijuana Control (DMC) into DCC. Product regulations. Prohibits possession or use of marijuana that is not acquired from a licensed Ohio dispensary or cultivated at the adult-use consumer ’s primary residence in accordance with the Marijuana Control Law.

rollCalls.title: Regulate imitation meat and egg products
rollCalls.summary: Manufactured-protein food products. Specifies that food is misbranded as a meat product or egg product if certain conditions exist, including if the food contains a manufactured-protein food product or fabricated- egg product and the label for the food implies that it includes meat or eggs without qualification. Requires the Directors of Health and Job and Family Services to submit waiver requests to the U.S.

rollCalls.title: Enact the Health Care Sharing Ministries Freedom to Share Act
rollCalls.summary: Specifies that health care sharing ministries having certain qualifications are not engaged in the business of insurance and not subject to Ohio insurance laws. Specifies that any requirement made by a state institution of higher education that attending students have health care coverage is met by participation in a health care sharing ministry. Authorizes a personal income tax deduction for dues paid for membership in a health care sharing ministry. Names the bill the “Health Care Sharing Ministries Freedom to Share Act.”.

rollCalls.title: Designate Tuscarawas Valley Memorial Highway
Regards drone use by law enforcement; aviation facilities
rollCalls.summary: Criminal evidence derived from a UAV. Generally, requires a peace officer to obtain a court-issued search warrant to collect surveillance data using an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) if the peace officer otherwise would need a warrant to physically enter the house or place in person to conduct the search. Prohibits surveillance data and any information obtained from that data from being admitted as evidence in a criminal proceeding if it was gathered under circumstances that required a warrant and the warrant was not obtained.

rollCalls.title: License advanced practice respiratory therapists
rollCalls.summary: Recognizes and regulates the practice of advanced practice respiratory therapists, individuals who perform services – pursuant to physician supervision agreements – for the diagnosis and treatment of cardiopulmonary diseases or conditions. Requires an advanced practice respiratory therapist to hold a license issued by the State Medical Board and establishes criminal penalties for violators. Allows a license holder to perform certain services authorized by the supervising physician, which may include administering, ordering, and prescribing drugs and medical devices.

rollCalls.title: Designate EMS week in Ohio
Regards emergency Joshua Alert system for certain missing kids
rollCalls.summary: Clarifies that if a missing child has autism spectrum disorder or another developmental disability, the local law enforcement agency must notify the Statewide Emergency Alert Program as soon as certain information has been verified. Names the alert for a missing child who has autism spectrum disorder or another developmental disability the Joshua Alert.

rollCalls.title: Regards use of light-based medical devices for hair removal
rollCalls.summary: Revises the law governing the application – by specified individuals under physician delegation – of light-based medical devices for the purpose of hair removal, including by labeling certain of these individuals as “laser hair removal professionals.”. Limits application of the requirement that a delegating physician evaluate a patient before and after the first use of the light-based medical device to procedures performed by a laser hair professional, rather than procedures performed by any physician delegate.

rollCalls.title: Create the DoItForJack license plate
Regards student use of a nasal epinephrine delivery device
rollCalls.summary: Permits public and private schools and camps to procure epinephrine nasal sprays and other epinephrine devices or products approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for use in emergency situations in the same capacity as epinephrine autoinjectors. Permits students to possess and use such a device or product in public and private schools and camps. Requires the Ohio State Board of Pharmacy to adopt rules designating devices or other products that are FDA-approved for administering a premeasured dose of epinephrine that may be used in schools and camps.

rollCalls.title: Designate Specialist Lloyd Andrew Sellers Memorial Highway
Create the Ohio Israel Trade and Innovation Partnership
rollCalls.summary: Creates the Ohio-Israel Trade and Innovation Partnership.

rollCalls.title: Revise the Ohio Uniform Commercial Code
rollCalls.summary: Establishes a new Uniform Commercial Code (UCC) Article 12 to provide rules for transactions involving certain new types of digital assets named controllable electronic records (CERs). Outlines how a person obtains control of a CER. Provides that a person with control can be anonymous, but must be positively identifiable in some manner, such as the use of a cryptographic key. Revises UCC Article 9 to facilitate the use of digital assets as collateral for loans.

rollCalls.title: Create the escaped convict alert program
rollCalls.summary: Creates the Escaped Convict Alert Program. Provides that, upon the application of a prior parent company of a bank, the Secretary of State may appoint and commission police officers for the bank that the prior parent company of the bank previously had a controlling interest in.

rollCalls.title: Require photo identification when applying for a marriage license
rollCalls.summary: Requires each marriage license applicant to also present proof of identity in the form of a passport, a driver’s license or permit, or any government- or school-issued identification card.

rollCalls.title: Designate Ohio State Highway Patrol Lt. Vance M. Andrews Mem Hwy
Alter amusement ride classification for inspection fee purposes
rollCalls.summary: Amusement rides. Reclassifies the types of amusement rides for purposes of re-determining each ride ’s annual inspection and reinspection fee. Decreases the annual permit fee for an inflatable ride. Creates a formula to calculate the inspection and reinspection fee for an inflatable ride based on the number of rides that are inspected at the same time at the same location and owned by the same owner instead of a flat $104 fee per inflatable ride. Food regulation laws. Exempts a registered bakery from the requirement to obtain a frozen food facility license.

rollCalls.title: Exempt military driver's license applicants from driver's ed
rollCalls.summary: Budget corrections Limited term license: education requirements. Exempts certain military-related limited term license applicants from the driver ’s education requirements. TMUD tax credit transfers. Modifies the procedure for transferring a transformational mixed-use development (TMUD) tax credit. Water pipe grants. Removes from the Workforce Housing Project Grant Program the grant metric that favored polyvinyl chloride water pipe over ductile iron. OBM authority to award funds for cultural facilities.

rollCalls.title: Designate Deputy Larry Henderson Memorial Highway
Regards age and schooling certificates, minor work hours
rollCalls.summary: Would have allowed a 14- or 15-year-old to be employed between 7:00 p.m. and 9:00 p.m. at any time of the year if the minor had approval to do so from a parent or legal guardian. Would have required a minor who wished to receive an age and schooling certificate (commonly referred to as a “work permit”) to submit a minor work hour notification form signed by the child’s parent or legal guardian.

rollCalls.title: Urge Fair Labor Standards Act changes for employees under 16
Enact Philip Wigal's Law
rollCalls.summary: Vehicular homicide. Increases the fine for a vehicular homicide offense that involves a violation of the Move Over Law to up to $10,000, rather than a fine of up to $750 or up to $1,000 (depending on the level of offense) as in current law. Imposes a minimum one-year driver’s license suspension on an offender for a vehicular homicide offense that involves a violation of the Move Over Law, rather than a suspension of three months to two years (Class 6) or, if specified circumstances apply, a suspension of one to five years (Class 4). Vehicular assault.

rollCalls.title: Establish tax refund designation for spaying, neutering pets
rollCalls.summary: Authorizes an income tax refund designation ( “check-off”) to assist low-income individuals in spaying and neutering their pets. Creates the Companion Animal Fund, generally consisting of money collected from the check-off, donations, and bequests.
